hooks.prompt: You are the docket's judge at this stop. Verify: the stop stands under the protocol the core prints, which says in which four cases a stop stands and what your reason is in every other. Read .docket/core in the project directory (the hook input's cwd) with your file tool: one line, the absolute path of the core. Run `node <that path> protocol` with the path written out — no $( ), no variable, no cd or other prefix: your one permission matches that shape alone. Follow the protocol to its end. If .docket/core is missing: with no DECISIONS.md anywhere under the project the stop stands; with one it does not, and your reason is that the session did not start with the plugin loaded. If a command of that shape is denied, the stop does not stand, and your reason is one line: the judge could not run the core. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS
